description: Plan step R4c (graph node rules). Enforce the peak levels: the stop level queues GLM subagents and pauses/resumes their goals (never the main agent), takeover on agent/created and resume on unload; the reduce level queues self-reported optional GLM spend through checkCall; the main agent's per-step peak line. Acts on host state (goals): deep review. Probe required. Depends on FEAT-007.
steps: Read rules design sec 3.6 (levels, the main agent line, wording), sec 6.3 stop-level paragraphs (pause goal, resume, let-once for the session this peak, restart takeover on agent/created, unload resume with the 2 s lock limit, activation takeover), sec 6.4 (main agent peak line in four wordings, wake text 'carry on' and the dispatch 'you may dispatch again' text), sec 15 R4 peak cases, V12 and V13 in the verification table. Read reference/dsh-desktop-0.2.1-rc.3 dsh-goal (pause/resume signatures {id, revision}, GoalError codes, revision bump on pause) and dsh-goal-round-driver (cancel only when the initiator is not this agent) in the MAIN checkout before coding.

Specs first (extend tests/rules-tickets.spec.ts, tests/rules-row.spec.ts, tests/fake-rc3.ts with goals.pause/resume recording calls and configurable GoalError, agent/created): stop level in a peak: the first tool call of a GLM subagent session opens a ticket with signature any:builtin:glm-peak-stop and pauses its active goal (record pausedGoal {id, revision after pause}); a main agent (GLM and non-GLM) and a non-GLM subagent are never touched, including propose_to_human-like tools and rules_show; main agent dispatching a GLM subagent gets an ordinary ticket from builtin:glm-peak-stop-dispatch that does not pause any goal and is woken with the 'dispatch again' text; pause throwing -> ticket pauseFailed with the first 80 chars, health degraded 'goal not paused', queueing continues; peak end (injected clock, 5 s) -> resume, 'carry on' wake, ticket done; resume throwing -> wake text carries the reason and tells the agent to inform the person, ticket still done, health degraded once; goal changed by the person (revision differs) -> no resume, only the wake; level changed stop -> inform resolves the same way; /rules let on a stop ticket sets letOnceUntil to the end of this peak (4 h when unreadable), calls pass until then, goal resumed; restart: new fake host, old heartbeat removed, agent/created takes over deferred/cleared tickets and host-gone tickets without resumedAt (ticket-adopt) and, if the peak is already over, resumes and wakes immediately; ordinary tickets are not taken over; unload resumes every stop ticket of this host that has pausedGoal and no resumedAt, writes ticket-update, sends no wake, a resume throw leaves the ticket for the next activation, and the whole unload step is bounded by 2 s; activation takes over live sessions the same way; reduce level: self-reported optional spend queues in a peak, necessary passes; main agent step reminder first line has the four wordings (stop/reduce/inform/unreadable), injected once at peak start, peak end and level change and not repeated within a peak, and a non-main agent's reminder has no such line; glm-peak unreadable -> nothing is held at any level.

Implement in src/rules/tickets.ts / index.ts / reminder.ts; add the minimal typed goal API to src/shared/dsh-min.ts (goals.get/pause/resume with their rc.3 shapes) with an AdapterContractCheck-style type check if an official .d.ts exists in the installed dev dependencies, otherwise cite the reference file and line in a comment; add peak-line text to the reminder; keep stateFor/stateForProject/peakHoldFor unchanged.

Probe: extend rules-peak (list default rule at the shifted clock; exactly one glm-peak-reminder notice and no rules-board copy of the pricing text; level line for the main agent says reduce / the default; no 'keep working' or 'postpone' strings from the board) and add rules-peak-stop (level preset to stop, probe verification plugin creates a goal for a GLM session; first tool call gets the stop text, goal becomes paused, no new round; /rules peak 无影响 as the human through the real handler; within 30 s the goal is active again and the request has the carry-on wake; a non-GLM session in the same scenario executes normally). Record V12 and V13 outcomes in findings.
Docs: ORCHESTRATION.md section 16 (levels, goal handling), DESIGN.md degradation table. Commit at most twice. Messages carry gate results including the probe exit code.
acceptance_criteria: No code path pauses, queues or denies the main agent at any level (tests for GLM and non-GLM main agents).
A paused goal is resumed on peak end, level change, let-once, takeover after restart and unload, and every failure leaves a ticket plus a health message that lets the person fix it by hand.
V12 and V13 are answered in findings with probe evidence (or stated as not verifiable with the reason).
Row still disabled; build, preflight, npm test and npm run probe exit 0 (or only the recorded baseline failures).

npm run probe exits 0 (rules-peak and rules-peak-stop included)

Verification answers (also in docs/ORCHESTRATION.md 16.13):
- V12 (pausing a goal in the gate does not interrupt the step): holds on the real runtime. The pause event came while the agent was running, the same step finished (its next request carries the refusal and it ended the turn), the goal stayed paused with the round count unchanged for 4 s, and after the plugin-side resume (from /rules peak 无影响 as the person) the driver started round 2 at once.
- V3 (inject to an idle agent with an active goal): not reached at L3. The round had already started when the wake was sent (the board writes the ticket first), so it went by steer and arrived in the step after. The inject path is covered by the fake host only.
- V13 (the unload runs on a normal exit and goals.resume works then): in the one-shot headless runner the row is not unloaded at exit (heartbeat file still there, goal paused, ticket deferred without resumedAt, nothing on stderr). That is the design's 'does not run' branch; the next start adopts the ticket (L2 tests). The desktop's normal quit was not verified (the desktop is not touched); the code does both: unload resumes, otherwise adoption on the next start. The scenario pins that the two outcomes agree.

Design points interpreted rather than followed (all in ORCHESTRATION.md 16.13):
1. A ticket handed to the dispatch root keeps its pausedGoal and nothing is resumed for it (the subagent's session has ended); resume acts only on a live subagent session, and a takeover by a new subagent does not pause a goal again when the ticket already has pausedGoal.
2. A stop ticket this process did not open (restart, activation, late heartbeat) is judged against a synthetic gate.tool-call event with role subagent and the session's own model, else a GLM stand-in model, since the original call is not stored.
3. The dispatch wake says 'You can dispatch again: <tool> "<summary>"': the design's task id and model have no source.
4. peakHoldFor, stateFor, stateForProject are unchanged, as the FEAT says; so peakHoldFor ignores a let (design 15 R4 says it should be undefined until the let ends). A later step can add it.
5. Not exercised by the specs: the 'reduce' entries in the gate (they hit only with glmSpend, which only checkCall carries; covered by tests/rules-check.spec.ts since FEAT-005) and the reminder of a subagent that is not holding a ticket.
6. The pricing service has no peakHours member, so the design's parenthesis (weekdays 14:00-18:00 UTC+8) is not in the refusal or the line (as in the earlier steps).
7. The peak line for 'stop' outside a peak ('GLM subagents and scripts that report GLM spending can run now.') is my wording; the design has examples for reduce and inform only.
8. The /rules peak reply no longer says there is no queueing: it says the level takes hold from the next tool call and dispatch.

Risks for the reviewer: (a) the pause happens before ticket-open; if the process dies between them the goal stays paused with no ticket (nothing adopts it; the person resumes by hand); the alternative order has the mirror gap. (b) The wake after a resume goes by steer in practice, one step late; the carry-on text says 'Your goal is resumed' while the round is already running. (c) Concurrent adopt (agent/created) and the 5 s pass is serialized only by reconcile's running flag: an adopt that finds a pass running leaves the judging to the next pass (at most 5 s). (d) docs/graph was not touched; the graph node rules has no record of these commits: the caller records them. (e) package-lock.json is untracked in the worktree and was never staged.
